text: Everything starts at Get Data in Power BI Desktop. Snowflake lives under the Database category, alongside Redshift and BigQuery — not a separate cloud bucket.

Two required fields, both about compute. Server, the account hostname. And Warehouse — whatever gets typed there is the compute footprint burning credits on every query this report runs. A cost decision, not just a connection string.

After authenticating, Navigator opens — database, schema, and table selection happens here. Select fct_orders and the customers mart. Nothing from staging or intermediate — Finance and Ops only need the business-facing layer.
The last step asks Import or DirectQuery. Use Import: fct_orders is already incrementally maintained in Snowflake itself, so a scheduled refresh after each dbt run is enough to keep this current.
Next lesson: building the Finance revenue page — revenue by day and by payment method, on top of the mart just connected.
